originality.rationale: The first-public 2019 primary test has uniformity for all reference sizes iff p=q and eventual detection for each alternative; this work establishes an explicit universal finite-support threshold, precise fixed-budget blind space, minimal sign changes with arbitrary-p extremizers, and exact first-visible response. Checked original full main text and proof appendix, searched semantic records and independent literature phrases. Classical total positivity and binomial mixtures are material residual coverage risks.
residual_risks: General identifiability or total-positivity literature on binomial mixtures may already imply the statements under a change of variables, without matching terminology.
A later detailed thesis or extended version of the 2019 test may include a finite-support refinement that was not materially inspected in full.
Rank-only and one-order tests are the stated domain; multiple orderings can increase information.

value.rationale: An exact common simulator-budget cutoff resolves whether a finite-alphabet goodness-of-fit procedure can ever gain power by increasing observations. The complete blind-space dimension and sharp ordered-sign obstruction distinguish smooth low-oscillation alternatives from worst-case oscillatory ones. The explicit example supplies nontrivial failure and first-visible calibration even for full-support nulls; no significance is attributed to mere computation or renaming.
